Legal template sites tend to assume that the only value lawyers add is providing documents. Lawyers still add value in negotiation and extracting salient points. Also, no liability is accepted for use of the documents on free sites.
There are significant differences in law between states (employment, corporate law). Would still have a licensed lawyer review these docs before executing them.

This is awesome, thanks Orrick team. Even if you don't use these verbatim, take a look at your current docs and then scan the Orrick version to see if any improvements occur to you. I'd like to see more law firms do this.
Awesome. Previously I'd been pointing people at Gunderson Dettmer's set of documents but it looks like Orrick's is more comprehensive.
Orrick has been hosting great events for entrepreneurs in the valley, all free—walking through key components of a term sheet, etc.

The documents have actually been up on Orrick's site for a while; I used these docs in 2010 to form my company. Even though I used Orrick to create these docs, I did not hire them when it was time for a lawyer.

I am a very happy customer of Orrick. They helped me tremendously with my incorporation (c-corp Delaware) and I attend their seminars frequently. These documents are great, but I recommend you go directly to Orrick. They also have wizards like the term sheet generator (tsc.orrick.com).
